title: Bakery-Style Blueberry Muffins
subtitle: tall, golden muffins bursting with wild blueberries and a sugar-crisp top
imageAlt: Tall golden blueberry muffins with sugar-crusted tops on a cream plate, one broken open, beside a navy napkin

beforeYouStart.text: Keep the blueberries frozen until the last second so they don't turn the batter purple.
Start hot at 220°C, then drop to 190°C: the burst of heat makes tall domes.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners.

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a large bowl.

steps.title: Wet
steps.text: Whisk the melted butter, eggs, milk and vanilla in a jug, pour into the dry and fold just until a few floury streaks remain.

steps.title: Berries
steps.text: Toss the frozen blueberries with the 1 tbsp flour and fold in with a few strokes. Fill the liners to the top and sprinkle with the sugar.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 5 minutes, then lower to 190°C (375°F) and bake 15–17 minutes more, until golden and a toothpick comes out clean. Cool 5 minutes in the tin.

fixIt.fix: Fill the liners right to the top and keep the 220°C start.
Use berries straight from the freezer and fold only a few strokes.
Overmixed; stop folding while you still see a little flour.

saleTip: No Frills wild blueberries (600 g) are often $5.49; they're smaller and spread through the muffin better.
swap: Raspberries or diced apple for blueberries. Buttermilk for milk.
leftovers: Freeze in a bag; microwave 20 seconds from frozen.
doneness: No meat; bake until a toothpick in the centre comes out clean and the tops spring back. The eggs are fully cooked by then.
source: Based on tested bakery-style muffin methods (King Arthur Baking, Canadian Living): melted-butter batter, frozen berries tossed in flour, filled to the top and started at high heat.
prepAhead: Whisk the dry mix the night before.
Baked muffins freeze up to 3 months.
reheat: Microwave 15–20 seconds, or 20 seconds from frozen; no food-safety reheat needed.

basic.note: Plain blueberry muffins; no vanilla or sugar top.

fancy.note: A cinnamon crumble on top instead of plain sugar.

addSteps.title: Crumble
addSteps.text: Rub the flour, brown sugar, cold butter and cinnamon together with your fingers into pea-sized crumbs. Make it before step 4 and pile it on the muffins in place of the sugar.

costAdd: Crumble: flour, brown sugar, butter, cinnamon
plating: Serve warm, split with a pat of butter.
Stack in a basket lined with a napkin.
Break one open to show the berries.

why.2-1: A light flour coat helps the berries stay suspended instead of sinking.
why.1-0: Melted butter gives a tender, rich crumb.

funFact: Canada is the world's largest producer of wild blueberries, most of them from Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Quebec and PEI.

keeps.thaw: Thaw on the counter 1 hour, or microwave 20 seconds from frozen

drink: Coffee or a cold glass of milk.
